subject: Evidence onboarding and collector instructions for Sentinel RFI
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sentinelsecurity.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@sentinelsecurity.com
Date: Fri, 1 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sentinel RFI: follow-up + logistics for control artifacts

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick overview yesterday. As promised, I'm circulating a consolidated list of the controls and artifacts our procurement/security team needs to close the RFI and move to a deeper SIG assessment. High level: we need a) control mapping (SOC 2 / ISO 27001) that points to evidence items, b) time-bounded logs (rotation, access reviews) for the last 12 months, and c) a single location where reviewers can pull files.

Attached is our internal checklist (sentinel-rfi-checklist.pdf) and an example of the export format we prefer. Can you confirm who on the Redwood side will be the evidence collector and the expected ETA for the first bundle? Also, any constraints on redacting customer data in logs would be useful.

Best,
Liam
Sentinel Security

Attachments: sentinel-rfi-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sentinelsecurity.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel RFI: follow-up + logistics for control artifacts

Liam —

Thanks for the checklist and the template. We're assigning Marissa to lead the evidence upload and Priyom to pull the runtime logs you requested. Quick plan:

- Deliverable A (by Wed 2028-09-06): Control mapping spreadsheet that links SOC 2 TSC and ISO 27001 clauses to Redwood controls and the exact artifact filename (control-mapping_v2.xlsx).
- Deliverable B (by Fri 2028-09-08): Compressed log bundles for the last 12 months (key-rotation-logs.tar.gz). Logs will be pre-scoped to platform-level operational events; we will redact customer identifiers where required and provide a redaction manifest.
- Deliverable C (by Fri 2028-09-08): Annotated SOC2 and ISO reports and a short readme that explains where each control's evidence came from (SOC2-report-2027.pdf, iso27001-annotated.pdf).

Two clarifications we need from you to finalize:
1) Which reviewer group needs access (security@sentinelsecurity.com or specific reviewer emails)?
2) Are there any legal or residency constraints for the artifact repository (must it be hosted in us-east-1 or acceptable on our secured drive)?

We'll create a shared Drive folder and post links once the first bundle is ready. If you prefer, we can also schedule a 30-minute handoff call when the artifacts are uploaded.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: control-mapping_v2.xlsx (stub)

From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@novacorp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sentinel RFI: follow-up + logistics for control artifacts

Hi team —

Novacorp will be participating in the SIG review as a downstream integrator. Two quick asks from legal/compliance:

- Please include a short manifest that lists which artifacts contain any customer-identifying fields and the method used for redaction.
- For key rotation logs, include the exact KMS aliases and a statement on key custody (who has admin privileges and how rotation is approved).

Also, for scheduling: our reviewer window is 2028-09-12 to 2028-09-16. If we can get an initial bundle by 2028-09-08, we can prioritize an early review.

Thanks,
Nora Patel
Sr. Security Manager, Novacorp

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sentinelsecurity.com>, Nora Patel <nora.patel@novacorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 Sep 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sentinel RFI: follow-up + logistics for control artifacts

Hi Liam / Nora —

We're on track to upload the first artifact bundle this afternoon. Summary of items you'll see in the Drive folder:

1) control-mapping_v2.xlsx — mapping tab for SOC 2 TSC (common criteria) and ISO 27001 clauses -> Redwood control owners -> artifact filenames.
2) SOC2-report-2027.pdf — audited report (redacted sections flagged in the manifest).
3) iso27001-annotated.pdf — certificate + annotated clauses.
4) key-rotation-logs.tar.gz — contains KMS alias list, rotation events (timestamps, operator IDs). Sensitive columns will be hashed; see redaction-manifest.txt in the same folder.

Access: we've invited security@sentinelsecurity.com and nora.patel@novacorp.com with view/download permissions. The drive is hosted in us-east-1 with our enterprise DLP controls applied. If you need a temporary elevated access window (download for reviewers), tell us the reviewer emails and we will schedule it.

Proposal for the handoff call: 2028-09-06 15:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite momentarily.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced in folder: redaction-manifest.txt (txt)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sentinelsecurity.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: nora.patel@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 6 Sep 2028 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel RFI: follow-up + logistics for control artifacts

Marissa —

Confirmed, thanks. I have access and downloaded the manifest to do a quick scope review. Two small follow-ups after a brief scan:

- In the control mapping spreadsheet, the row for encryption key custody (ISO A.8.2 / SOC2 CC7) references "key-rotation-logs.tar.gz" but doesn't call out who holds admin privileges. Can you add a short note in that row indicating the team (e.g., Platform Ops) and whether they are Redwood employees or a managed partner?
- For the rotation events, can you include the operational ticket ID that approved the rotation (if a ticket exists) or otherwise indicate the approval flow? That helps our audit trail.

If you can add those two data points before the handoff call, we should be able to move quickly into the SIG deep review next week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

-Liam
Sentinel Security
